Reconciled to existing /data nodes (not re-proposed): domain:formal-sciences, field:mathematics, field:statistics, subfield:linear-algebra, subfield:probability-theory, subfield:calculus, subfield:optimization. These existing nodes are listed in the reconciliation section of report.md.

Boundary decision: field:mathematical-logic is proposed as a level-1 field (not a subfield of mathematics) because MSC 2020 gives it section 03 at the same level as section 11 (number theory), section 51 (geometry), etc. This is flagged ambiguous because some universities treat it as a subdepartment of mathematics.

Boundary decision: subfield:logic exists in /data under domain:humanities (philosophy). Per generation-order instructions, philosophical logic is NOT re-proposed here. The mathematical logic sub-areas (set theory, model theory, proof theory, computability theory) are proposed as subfields of formal_sciences with cross-domain contamination flagged in uncertainty fields.

Boundary decision: CS-primary areas excluded — computational complexity theory, algorithm design, programming language theory, and type theory are out of scope (LCC QA75-76; MSC 68 primary). subfield:computability-theory is included at ambiguous:true because MSC files it under 03 (mathematical logic), not 68, and it predates CS as a discipline.

Boundary decision: subfield:cryptography and subfield:information-theory are included (ambiguous:true) because MSC 94 and LCC QA place them in mathematics, but QC should evaluate whether the CS continent is a stronger institutional home.

Granularity note: the order required coverage-completeness against MSC 2020 top-level sections. Several proposed nodes (sequences-and-series, special-functions, integral-equations, several-complex-variables, potential-theory, operator-theory, universal-algebra) have lower institutional visibility as standalone department-level areas but are included because MSC 2020 gives them peer top-level section status. QC should consider aggressive pruning of these.

Statistics subfields: the coverage-standard source (MSC 62) has over 20 sub-sections. The most commonly taught graduate-level areas have been proposed; highly granular areas (62H multivariate, 62M time series, 62N survival, 62J regression, 62K design) are included as individual nodes but flagged ambiguous — QC may prefer collapsing these into an 'applied statistics' umbrella.

subfield:decision-theory already exists in /data under domain:humanities (philosophy). A mathematics-side decision theory node (under optimization/operations research) could be warranted but risks duplication; this has been deliberately omitted pending QC guidance.

The two existing concept nodes (concept:random-variable, concept:probability-distribution) are level-3 and out of scope for this skeleton. Their QID grounding targets listed in the batch manifest are noted here for the resolver pass.
subfield:algebra and subfield:abstract-algebra overlap — QC should decide whether to keep both (elementary/abstract split) or merge. subfield:algebra is proposed as the broader umbrella.

subfield:applied-mathematics is proposed as a broad umbrella that overlaps with numerical-analysis, operations-research, control-theory, and mathematical-biology. QC should evaluate whether the umbrella node adds value or should be dropped in favor of its component sub-areas.
